chapter: Bands, leaders and radio of the thirties and forties
title: Johnny Williams, Bill Gussick and the Swing Club drummers
summary: Hutto contrasts Johnny Williams's all-over-the-drums style with Morehouse's subtler, more varied playing, and notes Bill Gussick in a Leith Stevens photo.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I guess one time you mentioned a drummer named Johnny Williams, do you remember him?

He was a real hell bent for leather. And one side of Chauncey's I guess Variety records, there's Johnny Williams playing it. 'I'll Build a Stairway to Paradise' the other side. He's all over the drums whereas Chauncey was a more subtle drummer and more variety whereas Johnny Williams really went at it. And I think Williams was on the Saturday Night Swing Club with Leith Stevens. And also Gussick was another drummer there.
I forget his first name. At least... There is a picture that we have here, Leith Stevens with
Chauncey and the N'Goma drums and there is another drummer in the background. I think that's Bill Gussick.
I think Chauncey did remark that he wished he could do like Johnny Williams did. I think Chauncey's work is more enduring.
